🔊 Iran demands end to selective IAEA statute implementation

📌 London, IRNA – On the 70th anniversary of the approval of the IAEA statute, Iran’s permanent mission to the UN in Vienna issued a statement calling for an end to the selective and politically motivated implementation of the Agency’s obligations.

The statement criticized the IAEA for applying double standards and discriminatory approaches, emphasizing that the Statute is a binding legal document and must not be used as a political instrument to serve the interests of certain powerful states.
​
Iran also condemned the unacceptable silence of the Agency’s governing bodies regarding the military attacks by the US and the Zionist regime on its peaceful nuclear facilities in 2025 and 2026. Furthermore, it highlighted the IAEA's failure to address the lack of comprehensive safeguards on the Zionist regime’s nuclear activities.
​
The Islamic Republic also called for the full, balanced, and non-discriminatory implementation of the IAEA Statute for all member states, particularly regarding technical cooperation and access to peaceful nuclear energy.
​
The full text of statement by the Iranian permanent mission in Vienna is as follows:
​
Permanent Mission of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the United Nations and other International Organizations in Vienna PRESS RELEASE On the Anniversary of the Approval of the IAEA Statute 23 October 2026 Seventy years after the adoption of the Statute of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) on 23 October 1956, a fundamental assessment is required as to the level and extent of the adherence to the principles and objectives of the Agency’s founding document.
​
This anniversary must therefore be more than an occasion for commemoration; it must serve as a moment of critical reflection, institutional accountability and a renewed commitment to the full, impartial and non-discriminatory implementation of the Statute.
​
The Statute: A Binding Mandate, Not a Political Instrument
​
The continued relevance of the IAEA Statute lies in the objective it establishes and the principles it enshrines. It implementation over the past seven decades has produced achievements in important areas. However, the failure to implement it fully, consistently, effectively and without discrimination, under all circumstances and with respect to all Member States, has caused the Agency to drift away from its core objective and priorities, undermine the principles governing its conduct, compromise its professionalism, and tarnish its authority and credibility.
​
The undeniable fact is that the Statute is the Agency’s constitution, not a document to be invoked selectively or interpreted according to the interests of powerful States or a group of States.
​
Beyond Safeguards: Upholding the IAEA’s Full Statutory Mandate
​
Article II establishes the Agency’s fundamental objective: to accelerate and enlarge the contribution of atomic energy to peace, health and prosperity throughout the world. Article III.A.1 requires the Agency to encourage and assist research, development and the practical application of atomic energy for peaceful purposes. Article III.B.3 further requires the Agency to allocate its resources efficiently to achieve the greatest possible general benefit, with due regard to the special needs of developing countries.
​
